title: Adiabatic Otto-like quantum thermodynamical cycle in the non-quasi-static regime
abstract: We show a finite-time Otto-like quantum thermodynamic cycle that preserves the adiabatic population structure of a time-dependent harmonic oscillator in the non-quasi-static regime. In the conventional energy representation, finite-rate driving induces non-adiabatic population redistribution and leaves residual excitations after the Hamiltonian has returned to its initial value. We show that this difficulty can be avoided by formulating the dynamics in the Lewis-Riesenfeld invariant representation, without modifying the physical Hamiltonian through auxiliary counterdiabatic driving. For a parametric Mathieu protocol, quantum inertia produces a mismatch between the spatial width of the working mode and its transient dressed energy scale. We propose an experimental implementation of this scheme in a trapped-ion Paul trap using stimulated Raman interactions, with independent control of the laser detuning and beam intersection angle. This provides a finite-time implementation in which the invariant population structure is preserved while the physical trap frequency evolves non-quasi-statically. Our results establish a clear distinction between adiabatic operation and quasi-static driving, providing a route toward finite-time quantum thermal cycles that retain the adiabatic energy structure without requiring the quasi-static limit.
summary: This paper develops a method to realize an Otto-like quantum thermodynamic cycle in a finite time without relying on the slow, quasi-static limit. It achieves this by reformulating the dynamics using the Lewis-Riesenfeld invariant representation, which prevents non-adiabatic energy loss. The theoretical framework is validated by proposing a detailed experimental implementation using a trapped-ion Paul trap.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of performing quantum thermodynamic cycles in a finite time, avoiding the need for the quasi-static limit while maintaining high efficiency.
main_result: By formulating the dynamics in the Lewis-Riesenfeld invariant representation, the authors demonstrate a method to preserve the adiabatic population structure during fast, non-quasi-static driving, thereby achieving finite-time quantum thermal cycles.
method: The core method involves using the Lewis-Riesenfeld invariant representation to describe the time evolution of a time-dependent harmonic oscillator, which circumvents the non-adiabatic population redistribution seen in conventional energy representations.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as a time-dependent harmonic oscillator undergoing an Otto-like quantum cycle. The dynamics are analyzed theoretically and proposed for experimental realization in a trapped-ion Paul trap using stimulated Raman interactions.
key_observables: Coefficient of Performance (COP), finite-time effectiveness ($\chi$), and the preservation of the adiabatic population structure.
important_parameters: The cycle operates in the non-quasi-static regime, involving parameters like the trap frequency variation ($\omega_M - \omega_m$) and the detuning/beam angle control in the trapped-ion setup.
main_assumptions: The analysis initially assumes unitary evolution (no dissipation) and relies on the ability to implement the cycle interactions in the invariant basis, which requires precise control over laser detuning and beam geometry.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison of the quantum Otto cycle path in different representations (quasi-static vs. non-quasi-static vs. invariant basis) and schematically detail the two required Raman beam configurations for the trapped-ion implementation.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from analyzing the general quantum properties of the TDHO, establishing the quasi-static thermodynamic framework, identifying the failure modes of fast non-quasi-static protocols, and finally proposing the invariant representation solution followed by the trapped-ion experimental realization.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it provides a concrete, experimentally viable pathway to circumvent the limitations of the quasi-static approximation in quantum thermodynamics, a key area bridging quantum optics and non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.

The initially relaxed wave packet with an ini- tial width ∆x ∼1 (in normalized units) undergoes severe localized compression in the non-quasi-static regime, peak- ing at the maximum squeezing point t3 = π/2, according to ∆x ∼σ(t), where the Ermakov parameter σ(t) is projected onto the lateral boundary plane (x = −2, dashed blue line) showing the direct causal link between the driving potential and the transient geometric narrowing of the quantum state before it unitarily breathes back to its initial configuration.

FIG. 5. Geometric schematic of the two Raman configura- tions required to implement the invariant-basis transitions at the two isochoric turning points. (Top) At the cold point t = 0, the unperturbed wave packet is spatially extended and the Raman beams intersect at the angle θC, with the corre- sponding spectral detuning δC. (Bottom) At the hot point t = π/2, quantum squeezing reduces the spatial width of the wave packet. The Raman configuration is therefore changed to the larger intersection angle θH, while the spectral detuning is simultaneously adjusted to the dressed energetic splitting Ω(t3).
